newsitem.title: USA: Archer - leave ethanol subsidy intact through 2000.
newsitem.headline: Archer - leave ethanol subsidy intact through 2000.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer Tuesday proposed changing the ethanol subsidy provision in his tax bill to leave the tax break intact through its expiration at the end of 2000.
The ethanol subsidy would then be eliminated after it expired, the Texas Republican said in proposing the change to his tax legislation before the House Rules Committee.
Originally, Archer's tax bill called for reducing the ethanol subsidy through the end of 2000, and then eliminating it after that.
Archer, a staunch critic of the ethanol subsidy, said he decided to change the tax bill provision in response to lawmakers who had protested the subsidy reduction.
"I believe that it's important that we take into consideration the views of a number of members who are very very concerned about this," Archer said.
"My major goal is to be sure that people get the message not to build new facilities in anticipation that this credit will be extended after the year 2000, it will not be extended," he said.
